what: PACK-ATTR and GEMM-OVERLAP (2026-10-18): where the bf16 GEMMs' packs stand inside the 9.84M decoder's training step at four threads after BF16-PANELS-1, and whether hiding them helps. A probe build times every pack task by role (the forward x W^T, the input adjoint dy W, the weight adjoint dy^T x) and operand (A, B), and each group's pack and compute phase walls; the same build with the untransposed B pack's two loops swapped (each tile written contiguously); and two builds that overlap the packs with the compute in one job a group -- per call (a compute task waits for every pack of its call and the calls before it) and per strip (a region waits for its own 32-row A strip and its columns' B strips where the layout allows, otherwise its operand's whole pack). Every comparison is two libraries alternated step by step in one process, the losses equal every round; scratch copies only (patches.py), the tree unchanged.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207: AMX-BF16 and AVX512-BF16; the guest sees four cores of one thread each; the instance of ../), GCC 13.3, -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno, Python 3.11.15; head e93f133 (runtime/c identical to 5804ad5's); bf16+exp+reduce+attn at four threads; indicative wall times, no PMU
reading: Inside the step (attribution-t4.json, the probe arm, 40 rounds) the packs take 8.15 ms of wall a step against 23.6 ms of AMX compute -- about a quarter of the GEMMs' time -- and their tasks 28.2 ms of thread time: the forward's A 2.86 and B (the weights) 4.85, the input adjoints' A 3.21 and B (the weights) 6.98, the weight adjoints' A 5.24 and B (the activations) 5.11; the weights' B packs are 42% of it, about 3.4 ms of the pack wall. Swapping the untransposed B pack's loops cuts those packs' task time by about 9% (the input adjoints' B 6.98 -> 6.36, the weight adjoints' B 5.11 -> 4.63) but the step reads x1.0194 (95% interval 0.997-1.036, the swap faster in 26 of 40): not resolved, not kept. Overlapping the packs with the compute is within noise per call (fused-t4.json: x1.002, 0.981-1.047, 31 of 60) and per strip (fine-t4.json: x1.0083, 0.991-1.031, 35 of 60): on this host the tile unit's compute and the packs do not overlap, so a pack has to be removed rather than hidden -- the weights' B panels, written when a weight is written, are the largest left.

files.run.sh: the records in order (bash run.sh OUT from the repository root): the copies, then the three comparisons at four threads
files.patches.py: the five scratch copies of runtime/c/bcir_tensor.c: base (unchanged), probe, swap (the probe with the B pack's loops swapped), fused (per call), fine (per strip)
files.pair.py: two libraries alternated step by step, the losses asserted equal every round: median steps, the paired ratio with a percentile-bootstrap interval, and where both carry the probe, the pack and compute walls and the pack tasks by role and operand
files.fused-t4.json, fine-t4.json: the shipped job against the two overlapped ones, 60 rounds each
